Name: Fire Resistance
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not inherently reduce the physical component of a Fire attack, smoke, environmental hazards, or Fire pair reactions.
Limits / Counterplay: Keep Burn resistance separate from heat-impact mitigation. Clearly signal resistance and distinguish reduced buildup, reduced ticks, delayed Ignition, and immunity.
Method: Reduces Burn buildup or Burn damage; delaying Ignition is a separate parameter and full immunity is a stronger explicit trait.

Name: Fearless
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not resist all Soul damage, essence drain, Silence, or other non-Fear effects.
Limits / Counterplay: Only applies to effects explicitly tagged Fear. Define the tier; full immunity is a stronger explicit version.
Method: Reduces Fear buildup, duration, or severity according to its tier.

Name: Membrane
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not automatically prevent statuses or hazards. An applying status is prevented only if the delivery hit is blocked under that attack's rule; existing statuses and persistent hazards remain.
Limits / Counterplay: Show shield damage and recharge clearly. Static recharge/supercharge must be bounded and cannot loop. Force resistance is measurable, not immunity.
Method: A separate shield pool absorbs eligible direct damage. After a short period without shield damage, it visibly regenerates. Force drains it less efficiently and causes less knockback while active; Static may rapidly recharge or supercharge it within a clear cap.

Name: Shell
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not inherently resist Burn/heat, Mucus adhesion, Bleed ticks, or Soul effects. It does not grant blanket status immunity.
Limits / Counterplay: Layers are lost permanently for the encounter and their loss must be visible. Keep fixed layer reduction distinct from Squishy's proportional reduction.
Method: Finite, non-regenerating armour layers each reduce qualifying physical hits by a fixed amount. Acid erodes/removes layers; sufficiently heavy Force can knock a layer loose.

Name: Bloodless
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not grant immunity to all Blood damage, physical wounds, or non-bleeding effects.
Limits / Counterplay: If an ability requires blood, it may fail or use an explicitly designed alternate effect. Do not silently turn Bloodless into universal Blood immunity.
Method: Prevents only effects that require usable blood or blood loss; direct Blood-type damage can still affect the target.

Name: Dodge
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not reduce damage after a hit, clear existing statuses, or erase persistent hazards. AoE edges may still hit and later contact with a hazard can still apply effects.
Limits / Counterplay: A clean miss prevents the hit and attached effects. Define attack-specific AoE and tracking rules; Mucus constrains movement only when the path crosses a sticky zone or the target is Adhered.
Method: Avoids an attack through movement/timing when positioning beats the hitbox and tracking rules.

Name: Squishy / Absorption
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not grant blanket status resistance or inherently reduce Acid, Static, Soul, heat/Burn, Mucus adhesion, Bleed ticks, or nonphysical effects.
Limits / Counterplay: Force is physical and qualifies. Keep proportional reduction distinct from Shell's fixed per-layer reduction; avoid extra hidden resistance rules.
Method: Proportionally reduces qualifying physical damage and may reduce physical impulse/knockback.

Name: Thorns
Does Not Automatically Protect Against: Does not retaliate against ranged attacks, remote hazards, non-contact effects, or attacks that cleanly miss due to Dodge.
Limits / Counterplay: Resolve one retaliation per attack hit, not per damage component. A successful Dodge prevents contact and therefore prevents retaliation. Bleeding/charged retaliation should be a named variant or weapon-combo effect.
Method: Returns damage once when a qualifying melee/contact hit connects. It does not reduce or prevent the incoming hit.
